objective: Make the theoretical skill and library objects reconstructable, answer-free, content-addressed and suitable for a label-independent description-length measurement without changing frozen method behavior.

alternatives.name: two-level canonical manifests with pinned closures
alternatives.reason: Separates one skill from one library version, preserves existing module boundaries, supports parent-linked rollback, and can reconstruct current behavior without copying third-party code or benchmark bodies.

alternatives.name: monolithic self-contained skill bundles
alternatives.reason: Simple to load but duplicates implementation bytes, complicates upstream rights, and risks treating vendored external code as first-party material.

alternatives.name: event ledger without loadable manifests
alternatives.reason: Preserves chronology but does not give one deterministic object for execution, rollback or description-length accounting.

canonicalization.json_rules: sort object keys, use compact separators, preserve array order only where semantically declared, reject duplicate keys and non-finite numbers
canonicalization.filename_rule: the terminal filename contains the computed digest; a content_sha256 field may repeat it only after independent recomputation
canonicalization.path_rule: repository-relative POSIX paths only; reject absolute paths, dot-dot segments, symlinks and root escape
canonicalization.publication_rule: exclusive terminal creation, no replacement, file fsync followed by directory fsync, and explicit abandoned-reservation recovery
canonicalization.compatibility_note: The existing llm4or.schema canonical function is a useful starting convention but is not by itself the new manifest validator or publisher.

skill_manifest.reference_shape: Every executable role names an interface, semantic version and ordered closure of repository-relative path plus SHA-256 pairs.
skill_manifest.provenance_shape: Authorship mode, parent proposal or source audit identity, construction split identity, verifier identity and admitted/rejected decision references; hashes and counts only, never benchmark or model-response bodies.
skill_manifest.semantic_payload_shape: A canonical declarative representation of guard conditions, typed grammar or DSL, transformation obligations, resource policy and fallback target. It may not be replaced by a short path or hash when computing description length.

library_manifest.skills_rule: Skill references are sorted by family and skill_id and bind the complete skill-manifest digest.
library_manifest.router_rule: The public-only router binds interface, implementation closure, zero/multiple-match fallback and overlap policy.
library_manifest.endpoint_rule: Bind endpoint schema, frozen plan and aggregate evidence identities without embedding evaluator-only answers.
library_manifest.transition_rule: A successor must bind its parent and rollback target. Failed promotion creates a rejected ledger event but no successor manifest.
library_manifest.genesis_rule: The genesis library uses null parent and rollback values and explicitly names the previous-system fallback.

description_length.primary_definition: Eight times the byte length of a prefix-free envelope containing the canonical semantic payload of every skill plus the canonical router semantic payload, ordered by manifest identity.
excluded: file paths and SHA-256 strings used only for reconstruction
timestamps, machine identifiers and elapsed time
benchmark identities, problem text and evaluator-only answers
description_length.anti_gaming_rule: A semantic payload cannot be replaced by a constant-size external pointer. Referenced first-party declarative bytes are included; third-party executable dependencies remain reconstruction dependencies and are not counted as learned knowledge.
description_length.validity_boundary: The payload grammar, prefix-free envelope and coding convention must be frozen before evaluated labels are opened. The current authored libraries do not retroactively satisfy this premise.

producer_compatibility.rule: Human authors, finite search, BIND, CoE, OptiTrust or another generator may propose the semantic payload, but all proposals enter the same manifest validator, verifier closure, resource admission and promotion endpoint.
producer_compatibility.same_artifact_same_decision: When two producers emit byte-identical canonical semantic payloads under the same manifest and verifier versions, admission must be identical.
producer_compatibility.non_guarantee: Producer compatibility does not guarantee that an output can be translated, passes admission or improves benchmark accuracy.

forbidden_fields: repair identity when redistribution is restricted
allowed_evidence: upstream repository URL, revision and license observation
aggregate correction, regression, abstention and failure counts
privacy_and_rights.external_code_rule: Unlicensed or separately licensed upstream code is referenced by source and revision and acquired separately; it is not embedded in the manifest bundle.

reconstruction_preflight: Validate canonical JSON, field allowlists, path containment and duplicate-free closure entries.
Recompute every first-party file hash before import or execution and again after reconstruction.
Resolve upstream dependencies only through separately disclosed reconstruction instructions and license checks.
Load the parent library and verify the rollback identity before constructing a successor.
Run the current direct-family and mixed identity checks without changing the frozen endpoint or opening restricted bodies.
Accept the manifest representation only if the reconstructed TSP, OR-Debug and mixed output hashes equal the sealed historical hashes.

closure_criteria.design: This document and its human-readable companion pass input-hash, internal-consistency, privacy-boundary and claim-boundary checks.
closure_criteria.implementation: A separately reviewed validator, exclusive publisher, current-library manifests and manifest-driven reconstruction reproduce all sealed hashes from a rights-safe clean clone.
closure_criteria.scientific: A future complexity-control experiment freezes this encoding before outcomes and compares valid library-selection units; manifest availability alone does not prove a complexity effect.
